Built for daily speed

One quiet workspace for everything you copy and write.

Stop digging through old tabs, lost chat messages, and overwritten clipboards. SnapNote keeps text, links, images, and notes organized right on your machine.

Smart Clipboard History

Every text snippet, URL, code block, and screenshot you copy is automatically captured, deduplicated, and indexed locally. Search across titles, body text, tags, and extracted image OCR text instantly with Ctrl+K.

Alt+X Floating Quick Access & Stay-on-Top

Tap Alt+X from any Windows app to pop up a compact, floating search palette. Copy what you need, tap again to hide — or pin the full frameless workspace above other windows whenever you're researching.

Rich-Text Notes

Write full notes with headings, bullet and numbered lists, interactive task checklists, blockquotes, syntax-friendly code blocks, undo/redo, and direct image paste.

Snippet Templates

Turn recurring emails, commands, or replies into reusable snippets using {{variables}}. Copying prompts for each blank while keeping your template intact.

Image Tools & Local OCR

Crop and annotate screenshots, pin reference images above other apps, and extract searchable text directly on your PC with optional Tesseract OCR.

Folders, Sessions & Favorites

Organize long-term projects in folders, group temporary research into sessions, and star favorites so clearing history never wipes out what matters.

Optional AES-256 Vault

Encrypt your entire local workspace at rest using AES-256-GCM and PBKDF2-SHA256. Lock in one click to halt clipboard capture and close pinned images instantly.

Privacy by architecture

Your clipboard touches everything you do. It should never leave your PC.

Passwords, API keys, private drafts, screenshots, and personal messages pass through your clipboard every day. SnapNote is built on a simple rule: there is no backend server, no login, and no telemetry SDK.

Data is stored locally in transactional IndexedDB inside your Windows profile. Turn on live encryption to lock everything with AES-256-GCM and PBKDF2-SHA256, or pause automatic capture in one click before copying sensitive items.

Answers

Frequently asked questions

Does SnapNote need the Visual C++ Redistributable or anything else installed?

No. SnapNote statically links the C runtime in its Windows builds, so the MSI and setup.exe installers run on a clean Windows 10 or 11 machine out of the box. The only optional extra is Tesseract if you want offline OCR text extraction inside images.

Where is my clipboard and notes data stored?

Everything lives inside local transactional storage in the app's device profile on your PC. There is no cloud sync, no account, and zero telemetry. Backups are created only when you explicitly export them.

Does Alt+X still work after I close the SnapNote window?

Yes. Closing the window minimizes SnapNote to the Windows system tray so Alt+X remains ready globally. Choosing Quit SnapNote from the tray menu exits the app completely.

Can SnapNote extract text from screenshots offline?

Yes. Install Tesseract OCR once and add it to your Windows PATH. SnapNote runs recognition locally on your machine and stores extracted text as searchable metadata without uploading images anywhere.

How does SnapNote workspace encryption work?

You can enable optional live vault encryption in Settings. SnapNote encrypts stored clips, notes, and images using AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2-SHA256 key derivation. Your password is never stored or transmitted, so keep a secure copy and an encrypted backup.

Why does Windows SmartScreen show a prompt on first install?

SnapNote is an independent, free open-source project and its Windows installers are currently unsigned. Every release is built in a public GitHub Actions pipeline and ships with SHA-256 checksums so you can verify the exact file before installing.

Is my data from an older version of SnapNote compatible?

Yes. On first launch, existing rich-text notes migrate cleanly into the workspace store while retaining a recovery copy of legacy records.

Is SnapNote available for macOS or Linux?

SnapNote is built with Tauri v2 and Rust, and prebuilt installers are currently tested and released for Windows 10 and Windows 11 (x64). Developers can inspect or build from source in the public GitHub repository.
